en.title: Nice to Monaco
en.excerpt: French riviera, manageable climbs, a few roadside stretches and a €12/day poolside finish in Monaco.
en.body:
In **2023**, I ran from near **Nice airport to Monaco**, where my Strava screenshot records **25.80 km**. From the promenade in Nice all the way to Monaco, the views were excellent. There were climbs and a few sections where I needed to pay attention to the road, but nothing I found impossible compared to some other places. The run ended with a sun lounger beside a proper outdoor pool in Monaco. The weather was on my side too. 

## Start: the Nice promenade

I started near the airport and made my way along Nice's promenade. This was the most straightforward part of the run, and it felt very flat and safe. The sea was right there - easy place to settle into the run.

## Hills, roadside sections and a useful drink stop

Once I was away from the promenade, the route became more varied. There were climbs, but they were manageable. Some sections ran beside the road between the hills, so I had to be more careful there than on the promenade. I also ran past **Cap Roux**, another beautiful spot on this stretch of the coast.  There was also a petrol station around halfway to Monaco, where I could buy a quick drink and use bathroom. French riviera is a beautiful thing and most of the time during the run, I was just enjoying the views.

## The coastal path into Monaco

On the approach to Monaco, I followed a beautiful stretch by the sea, with the path running between the rocks. It was a lovely way to arrive after the road sections and the hills. This was also the most pleasant place for an easy jog in Monaco(also heard that locals in Monaco use these cliffside paths for running). 

![The rocky coastal path at Cap-d'Ail beside the Mediterranean](/assets/uploads/nice-to-monaco/cap-dail-coastal-path.jpg "The coastal path at Cap-d'Ail.")

Photo: [Renek78 / Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Littoral_path_between_Plage_de_la_Mala_and_Plage_Marquet_in_Cap-d%27Ail_01.jpg), [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/).

## Monaco: a poolside finish

Inside Monaco itself, running is more awkward. The tourist crowds and narrow streets made it difficult to settle into a rhythm. Fortunately the city was getting into F1 rhythm and the main start-finish straight was closed for traffic - so I grabbed the opportunity and used it for running. 

I finished by the pool in Monaco. On my 2023 visit, €12 covered a shower and the chance to spend the rest of the day on a sun lounger beside the pool**** (friend visited the same place few months ago in 2026 and confirmed the same, bang for the buck price)**.** A very good end to the run. The pool itself was olympic size-large and very well kept. I noticed several people with Ironman backpacks there for swim training. For a future visit, check the [municipality's pool information](https://mairie.mc/le-stade-nautique-rainier-iii).

As I already mentioned, preparations for the Formula 1 race were underway when I arrived in Monaco. A good place to have a ice cream:

![Me eating an ice cream in Monaco, with Grand Prix preparations behind me](/assets/uploads/nice-to-monaco/monaco-ice-cream.jpg "An ice cream in Monaco after the run, with F1 preparations in the background.")

## My Strava and the Garmin route

The screenshot below is from my activity. It records **25.80 km** and a pace of **4:32/km**. You can click it to open [my Strava profile](https://strava.app.link/W1a7SCITG7b).

![My Strava screenshot showing the Nice to Monaco route, 25.80 km and 4:32 per kilometre](/assets/uploads/nice-to-monaco/strava-activity.jpg "My Strava activity screenshot. Click to open my profile.")

![The supplied Garmin GPX course plotted from Nice to Monaco](/assets/uploads/nice-to-monaco/garmin-course.svg "Route line from the Garmin GPX file supplied with this story. No street basemap is shown.")

The GPX course line measures approximately **25.30 km**, while the Strava activity screenshot shows **25.80 km**. I have kept the two figures separate. The original **Garmin GPX file** is available to download below.

## Would I do it again?

For the views, yes. I would keep the same distinction in mind: **Nice's promenade felt very easy**, while the roadside stretches between the hills needed more attention. The climbs were manageable, and the scenery made the effort worthwhile. This was a run where the surroundings were a big part of the point. 

**Top 3** of all the placese where I've ran.
